Guillermo's own take for Mon, Oct 26 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): The outflow is on its way out. Pam Rocks read N 21 at 7am, down from 30 at 2am but still ahead of the page’s 18. Pemberton is still 4 hPa above Vancouver, which usually keeps it blowing a few more hours.

Porteau is a maybe until about 10am, on the ebb from 14.9ft. If Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north at 8am, go. Under 20, stay home.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 AM PDT 26 October 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Tuesday. Gale warning in effect. Wind becoming light this evening then increasing to southerly inflow 10 to 20 near noon Tuesday.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 AM PDT 26 October 2026): Today Tonight and Tuesday. Wind northwest 10 to 20 knots diminishing to light near noon then becoming southeast 5 to 15 early this evening. Wind becoming northwest 15 near midnight then diminishing to light Tuesday afternoon. Wind increasing to southeast 10 to 20 Tuesday evening.
